examples.ko: 오랫동안 방치된 건물이 동네의 흉물이 됐어요.
examples.en: The building left abandoned for so long has become an eyesore in the neighborhood.
That statue was criticized as an eyesore.
The abandoned building remains an eyesore, so residents are worried.

examples.ko: 시에서 흉물 같은 철탑을 철거하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The city decided to tear down the hideous steel tower.

examples.ko: 공사가 멈춘 채 흉물처럼 서 있는 아파트가 많아요.
examples.en: There are many apartment buildings standing like eyesores with construction halted.

examples.ko: 낙서 때문에 멀쩡한 벽이 흉물은 아니어도 지저분해 보여요.
examples.en: Because of the graffiti, a perfectly fine wall looks messy, even if not a real eyesore.

explain: 뉴스에서 '흉물로 방치되다'처럼 건물이나 시설이 흉하게 남아 있을 때 많이 써요. 사람에게 쓰면 아주 심한 욕이 되니 건물·시설·물건에만 쓰는 게 좋아요.
explain_en: In the news it often appears as '흉물로 방치되다' for buildings or facilities left in an ugly state. Using it for a person is a very harsh insult, so use it only for buildings, facilities and objects.

en: lean crop; bad harvest; bad crop

examples.ko: 올해는 가뭄 때문에 사과 농사가 흉작이에요.
examples.en: This year the apple harvest is poor because of the drought.
Because of the bad harvest, rice prices went up a lot.

examples.ko: 태풍이 두 번 지나가서 흉작을 걱정하고 있어요.
examples.en: Two typhoons passed through, so people are worried about a bad harvest.
Last year the harvest was bad, but I hope this year's will be a bumper one.
The bad harvest deepened the farmers' sighs.
I heard the cabbage harvest is bad because of the weather.

explain: 반대말은 '풍작'이고, '흉작이 들다'처럼 많이 써요. 농사 이야기나 뉴스에서 주로 나오고, 일상 대화에서는 '농사가 안 됐어요'라고도 말해요.
explain_en: Its opposite is '풍작' (bumper harvest), and it is often used as '흉작이 들다'. It mostly appears in farming talk and the news, while in daily speech people may also say '농사가 안 됐어요'.

examples.en: The graffiti drawn on the wall is so hideous.

examples.ko: 어두운 방에서 흉측한 그림자가 보여서 놀랐어요.
examples.en: I was startled to see a hideous shadow in the dark room.

examples.ko: 그 벌레의 모습이 흉측해서 눈을 돌렸어요.
examples.en: That bug looked so gross that I turned my eyes away.

examples.ko: 영화 속 괴물이 생각보다 흉측하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The monster in the movie wasn't as hideous as I expected.
After the construction, the building became even uglier.

examples.ko: 흉측하게 부서진 인형을 보고 아이가 울었어요.
examples.en: The child cried upon seeing the horribly broken doll.

explain: 보기 싫은 정도가 강해서 징그럽거나 섬뜩한 느낌이 들 때 써요. '못생기다'보다 훨씬 센 말이라 사람의 외모에 쓰면 아주 무례해요.
explain_en: It is used when something looks so bad that it feels gross or creepy. It is much stronger than '못생기다' (ugly), so using it about a person's looks is very rude.

examples.en: These days an unsettling rumor is going around the neighborhood.
As the incidents continued, public sentiment became uneasy.
The mood is so uneasy that I'm afraid to go out at night.
Don't believe the ominous stories that have spread around.
The world feels unsettled, so make sure to lock up well.

examples.ko: 회사가 어렵다는 말에 사무실 분위기가 흉흉해요.
examples.en: After hearing the company is in trouble, the mood in the office is tense.

explain: 소문, 민심, 분위기, 세상처럼 사람들이 불안하고 뒤숭숭할 때 써요. 사람의 성격이나 얼굴을 말하는 말이 아니라 주변 분위기를 말해요.
explain_en: It is used for rumors, public sentiment, mood or the world when people feel anxious and unsettled. It describes the surrounding atmosphere, not a person's character or face.

examples.en: A quiet sob could be heard from inside the room.
The trembling voice turned into sobbing.
I bit my lip to hold back my sobs.
The sound of sobbing came from all over the theater.
The child spoke in a voice mixed with sobs.
The sobbing that went on all night stopped at dawn.

explain: 소리 내어 크게 우는 '울음'과 달리, 어깨를 떨며 낮게 숨죽여 우는 소리예요. 동사는 '흐느끼다'이고, 소설이나 이야기에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Unlike '울음' (loud crying), it is a low, held-back sound of crying with trembling shoulders. The verb is '흐느끼다', and the word often appears in stories and novels.

examples.en: The willow branches sway slowly in the wind.
The dancers swayed limply to the music.

examples.ko: 너무 피곤해서 몸이 흐느적거리는 것 같아요.
examples.en: I'm so tired that my body feels like it's wobbling.
Seaweed moves, swaying gently, in the water.
He came walking with his arms swinging loosely.
The inflatable figure flopping in the wind was funny.

explain: 힘없이 부드럽게 늘어져 흔들리는 모습에 써요. '흐느적대다'도 같은 뜻이고, 사람이 기운 없어 보일 때도 써요.
explain_en: It describes something hanging softly and swaying without strength. '흐느적대다' means the same, and it can also be used when a person looks drained of energy.

examples.en: The cherry blossoms are in full bloom in the park.
I took photos while walking along the path of blossoms in full bloom.
The roses are blooming profusely in the yard, so it is full of fragrance.
Butterflies flit among the flowers in full bloom.
The azaleas are in splendid full bloom this year.
At the feast, people had a wild, lively time.

explain: 꽃이 탐스럽게 활짝 핀 모습에 가장 많이 쓰고, 보통 '흐드러지게 피다'로 말해요. 잔치나 놀이가 한창 무르익은 분위기를 말할 때도 '흐드러지게 놀다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is used most often for flowers blooming lushly and fully, usually as '흐드러지게 피다'. It can also describe a party or play at its liveliest, as in '흐드러지게 놀다'.

examples.en: I couldn't sleep, so my eyes look dull and unfocused.
I went into the meeting in a foggy state of mind.
He ended up giving a vague answer.
After taking the medicine, my head became foggy.
His attitude is so unclear that I don't know what he means.
That person's explanation stayed vague to the very end.

explain: 정신, 눈빛, 기억, 태도가 또렷하지 않을 때 써요. '흐리다'가 날씨나 유리에도 쓰이는 것과 달리, 이 말은 주로 사람의 상태나 태도에 써요.
explain_en: It is used when someone's mind, gaze, memory or attitude is not sharp or clear. Unlike '흐리다', which also fits weather or glass, this word mostly describes a person's state or attitude.

examples.en: I boiled it too long, so the noodles turned mushy.
In the heat, the ice cream melts into a soft mess.
My legs gave out and I collapsed limply.
The rain-soaked paper went soft and fell apart.
The tofu crumbled mushily, so I put it into the stew.
The boiled eggplant drooped limply.

explain: 단단하지 않고 물러서 형태가 무너지는 느낌이에요. 국수나 채소 같은 음식, 젖은 물건, 힘 빠진 몸에 두루 쓰고, 형용사 '흐물흐물하다'와 짝이에요.
explain_en: It conveys something soft rather than firm, losing its shape. It fits food like noodles and vegetables, wet objects and a body that has lost strength, and it pairs with the adjective '흐물흐물하다'.

en: be squishy; be mushy; be squashy; be limp

examples.en: The overripe banana is mushy.
The noodles are mushy, so they don't taste good.
It's better to throw away fruit that has gone mushy.
After soaking for so long, my fingers went wrinkly and soft.
Flip the tofu gently so it doesn't fall apart.
I caught a cold, so my body feels weak and limp.

explain: 음식에 쓰면 면이 퍼졌거나 과일이 너무 물러서 별로라는 느낌이 있어요. 반대로 식감이 좋을 때는 '쫄깃하다'나 '단단하다'를 써요.
explain_en: For food it carries a negative feel, such as noodles that have gone soft or fruit that is too ripe. For good texture, people say '쫄깃하다' (chewy) or '단단하다' (firm) instead.

examples.ko: 처음엔 열심히 하더니 프로젝트가 흐지부지돼 버렸어요.
examples.en: They worked hard at first, but the project just fizzled out.
The promised repair petered out, so I inquired again.
My diet plan fizzled out before I knew it.

examples.ko: 회의에서 나온 이야기가 흐지부지될까 봐 걱정돼요.
examples.en: I'm worried that what was discussed in the meeting will come to nothing.
The club meetings are gradually fading away.

examples.ko: 이번 사건 조사가 흐지부지되면 안 돼요.
examples.en: The investigation of this case must not just fizzle out.

explain: 끝맺음이 분명하지 않게 슬그머니 사라질 때 써요. 일상에서는 '흐지부지 끝나다', '흐지부지 넘어가다'처럼 부사 '흐지부지'로도 많이 말하고, 계획·약속·조사·모임에 잘 어울려요.
explain_en: It is used when something fades away without a clear ending. In daily speech people also use the adverb '흐지부지' as in '흐지부지 끝나다' or '흐지부지 넘어가다', and it suits plans, promises, investigations and meetings.

en: leave vague or half-done; gloss over

examples.en: If you leave work half-done and vague, you lose trust.
He always leaves his assigned tasks vaguely unfinished.
He did his homework sloppily and went out to play.
The problem was brushed aside, so it eventually got bigger.

examples.ko: 약속을 흐지부지하지 말고 분명히 말해 주세요.
examples.en: Please don't be vague about the promise; tell me clearly.
I have many plans that I started and left hanging.

explain: 일을 분명히 마무리하지 않고 얼버무리거나 대충 끝내는 것을 말해요. 저절로 슬그머니 사라지는 건 '흐지부지되다'라고 하고, 일상에서는 '흐지부지 넘어가다'처럼 부사로 더 자주 써요.
explain_en: It describes leaving something vague or half-done instead of finishing it properly. When something fades away by itself, use '흐지부지되다', and in daily talk the adverb is more common, as in '흐지부지 넘어가다'.

examples.en: The child scattered toys all over the room.
The wind messes up my hair.

examples.ko: 큰 소리가 집중을 흐트러뜨리지 않게 조심하세요.
examples.en: Be careful that loud noises don't break your concentration.

examples.ko: 정리한 책을 또 흐트러뜨리면 안 돼요.
examples.en: You must not mess up the books I arranged again.
He left, strewing clothes here and there.
There were many things that could unsettle my mind.

explain: 정돈된 것을 일부러든 실수로든 어지럽게 만들 때 써요. 저절로 어지러워지면 '흐트러지다'라고 하고, 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요. '흐트러트리다'도 같은 뜻으로 써요.
explain_en: It is used when you make something that was neat messy, on purpose or by accident. When it becomes messy by itself, use '흐트러지다', so learn them as a pair. '흐트러트리다' is also used with the same meaning.

examples.ko: 선거 때마다 상대 후보에 대한 흑색선전이 나와요.
examples.en: Every election, smear campaigns against the opposing candidate appear.
Don't fall for smear tactics; check the facts.
There's a rumor that a rival company spread a smear campaign.

examples.ko: 그 후보는 그 소문이 모두 흑색선전일 뿐이라고 해명했어요.
examples.en: The candidate explained that the rumor was nothing but a smear campaign.

examples.ko: 흑색선전 때문에 후보가 큰 피해를 입었어요.
examples.en: The candidate suffered great damage because of the smear campaign.

examples.ko: 근거 없는 흑색선전은 처벌받을 수 있어요.
examples.en: Baseless smear campaigns can be punished.

explain: 상대를 깎아내리려고 근거 없는 거짓 소문을 퍼뜨리는 일을 말하고, 주로 선거나 정치 뉴스에서 나와요. 비슷한 말로 '비방'이 있고, 요즘은 '네거티브'라고도 해요.
explain_en: It refers to spreading baseless false rumors to bring down an opponent, and mostly appears in election and political news. A similar word is '비방' (slander), and these days people also say '네거티브' (negative campaigning).

examples.ko: 그 사람은 뭔가 흑심이 있는 것 같아요.
examples.en: That person seems to have some ulterior motive.
He pretends to be kind, but he harbors a hidden agenda.

examples.ko: 저는 아무 흑심 없이 도와준 거예요.
examples.en: I helped without any ulterior motive.

examples.ko: 그가 갑자기 잘해 주는 건 흑심 때문일지도 몰라요.
examples.en: His sudden kindness may be because of a hidden motive.
His ulterior motive was soon revealed.
The offer was full of ulterior motives, so I refused it.

explain: 남을 속이거나 이용하려는 음흉한 속마음을 말해요. '흑심을 품다', '흑심이 있다'처럼 쓰고, 친한 사이에서는 장난으로 '무슨 흑심이야?'라고 묻기도 해요.
explain_en: It means a sly inner intention to deceive or take advantage of someone. It appears as '흑심을 품다' or '흑심이 있다', and among close friends people may playfully ask '무슨 흑심이야?'.

examples.ko: 아이는 엄마를 보자 흑흑 울기 시작했어요.
examples.en: The child started sobbing as soon as she saw her mother.

examples.ko: 방에서 누가 흑흑 소리 내며 울고 있어요.
examples.en: Someone in the room is crying with sobs.
My friend sobbed, saying she failed the exam.
Sob, sob, my beloved puppy is gone!

examples.ko: 드라마를 보다가 나도 모르게 흑흑 울었어요.
examples.en: While watching a drama, I found myself sobbing.

examples.ko: 그는 한참을 흑흑 흐느끼다가 겨우 말을 꺼냈어요.
examples.en: He sobbed for a long while before he could finally speak.

explain: 우는 소리를 흉내 낸 말이에요. 크게 우는 '엉엉'과 달리 숨을 삼키듯 작게 우는 느낌이고, 채팅에서는 슬픈 척 장난스럽게 쓰기도 해요.
explain_en: It imitates the sound of crying. Unlike '엉엉', which is loud crying, it feels like quiet sobbing with held breath, and in chats people also use it jokingly to act sad.

examples.en: My younger sibling was angry and shot me a sideways glare.
Don't glare at me; say it with words.

examples.ko: 그는 옆자리 사람을 흘겨보며 한숨을 쉬었어요.
examples.en: He sighed while glaring at the person next to him.
Mom shot me a sideways glare, so I closed my mouth.

examples.ko: 사람들이 늦게 온 저를 흘겨보는 것 같았어요.
examples.en: It felt like people were glaring at me for coming late.

examples.ko: 친구가 장난으로 저를 흘겨보면 웃음이 나요.
examples.en: When my friend playfully glares at me, I laugh.

explain: 못마땅하거나 밉거나 화가 나서 눈동자를 옆으로 돌려 쳐다볼 때 써요. 그냥 '쳐다보다'와 달리 감정이 담겨 있고, '눈을 흘기다'도 비슷하게 말해요. 슬쩍 한 번 보는 '흘끗 보다'와는 달라요.
explain_en: It is used when you look at someone sideways out of displeasure, dislike or anger. Unlike plain '쳐다보다', it carries emotion, and '눈을 흘기다' is a similar expression. It differs from '흘끗 보다', which means a quick glance.
